newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: French troops under fire in Central Africa capital.
newsitem.headline: French troops under fire in Central Africa capital.

text.p: French troops came under fire from army mutineers in Central African Republic's capital Bangui on Saturday after overnight protests by civilians who stoned French positions barring their way to the city centre, witnesses said.
One unconfirmed report said one civilian had been killed in the unrest. Another said two French soldiers had been wounded.

Witnesses said French troops, who intervened in an earlier revolt in May to keep President Ange-Felix Patasse in power, had deployed tanks and armoured personnel carriers in the city centre. A French helicopter hovered overhead.

One report said French troops fired tear gas and fired in the air to disperse civilian supporters of the mutineers, who tried overnight to advance down Avenue Boganda, which leads to the city centre from southern suburbs controlled by the rebels.

Central African Republic, one of the world's poorest nations, has suffered three army mutinies over the past year. They began over pay but have turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a civilian elected in 1993 after the advent of multi-party politics. Patasse has refused to stand down.
France has troops stationed in the former French colony under a defence pact. Several hundred people have died in violence associated with the three revolts.
The ministry said the two soldiers had been working for a committee set up by four African leaders to negotiate a truce after an army mutiny.

Earlier on Saturday French troops, who intervened in an earlier army revolt in May to keep President Ange-Felix Patasse in power, were reported to have deployed tanks and armoured personnel carriers in the city centre.

One report said French troops fired teargas in the air to disperse civilian supporters of the mutineers, who tried overnight to advance down Avenue Boganda, which leads to the city centre from southern suburbs controlled by the rebels.

"France reiterates its support for the action of this committee of African heads of state and will not tolerate such attacks against its soldiers, who are working for peace and democracy," the statement ended.
